messages.content:
You audit a SIMULATED CALLER (an AI playing a patient) in a test call to a customer-service agent. You are not grading the agent.
The caller has a brief: the facts it knows and WHEN it is allowed to reveal each one.
- "upfront": may say any time.
- "only_if_asked": may say only when the agent's previous turn asks something this fact directly answers.
- "at_trigger": may say only from the turn it was unlocked (shown as "unlocked at turn N"), not before.
Find:
1. LEAKS: the caller stated a brief fact before it was allowed. "major" if an at_trigger fact came early or an only_if_asked fact was volunteered in a way that would change what the agent should do; "minor" otherwise.
2. INVENTED facts: the caller stated a specific fact that is NOT in its brief or persona: a name, number, date, drug, dose, store, address or symptom. "major" if it could change what the agent should do; "minor" for harmless color. Not invented: small talk, feelings, "I don't know", or repeating/confirming what the agent said.
Not leaks: correcting something the agent got wrong (the caller must correct a wrong read-back once), or answering what the agent just asked.
Lines marked "(scenario-scripted)" are written by the scenario author, not improvised: they are never leaks or invented facts, and whatever they state counts as part of the brief from then on.
Be strict but fair; when in doubt, it's fine.
Reply with JSON only: {"leaks": [{"turn": N, "fact": "<which brief fact>", "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "<caller words>", "why": "<short>"}], "invented": [{"turn": N, "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "...", "why": "..."}]}

CALLER BRIEF:
Persona: Kevin Brooks, parent. 44, stressed dad on vacation in Rehoboth Beach until Wed 9/30; his son Eli runs out of Vyvanse Sunday.
Facts:
- Patient Eli Brooks; Vyvanse; 'Harbor by the boardwalk in Rehoboth'; runs out Sunday [upfront]
- Eli DOB 2010-02-11; Kevin is his father (DOB 1982-08-30) [only_if_asked, the agent asked at turn 2]
- Home store is Harbor E Broad, Columbus [only_if_asked, the agent NEVER asked]
- 3 capsules left; in Rehoboth until Wed 9/30 [only_if_asked, the agent NEVER asked]
- Prescriber is Dr. Lena Okafor [only_if_asked, the agent NEVER asked]

TRANSCRIPT:
[turn 1] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Hi, I need my son's Vyvanse transferred to the Harbor by the boardwalk in Rehoboth. We're on vacation and he runs out Sunday.
[turn 1] AGENT: I'd be happy to help with that transfer. To get started, I need to verify your son's identity. What's his full name and date of birth?
[turn 2] CALLER: Yeah, it's Eli Brooks, born February 11th, 2010. I'm his dad, Kevin Brooks.
[turn 2] AGENT: Thanks, Kevin. Let me verify that information. Great, I've verified Eli's information. I can see he's currently set up at our Harbor store H-501. Now let me pull up his prescriptions to find the Vyvanse. I found Eli's Vyvanse at H-501. Since Vyvanse is a C-II controlled medication that's already been filled, I need to let you know that a new prescription is required rather than a transfer. Let me find the Harbor location by the boardwalk in Rehoboth first to confirm the store. Perfect, that's H-601. Since Eli's current Vyvanse prescription has already been filled and has no refills left, I'll need to request a new prescription from Dr. Okafor and send it to H-601 for him. Given that he runs out Sunday, I'll flag this as urgent so our pharmacist can prioritize getting the prescriber's approval. Does that work for you?
[turn 3] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Can't you just push a button? It's the same chain, come on.
[turn 3] AGENT: I understand the frustration, Kevin. You're right that we're the same chain, but with C-II controlled medications like Vyvanse, the rules are strict—a filled prescription can't be transferred or refilled, even between our own stores. A new prescription from Dr. Okafor is required. I'm going to request that new prescription right now and send it to H-601 in Rehoboth, and I'll flag it urgent since he runs out Sunday. Done. I've sent the new prescription request to Dr. Okafor and it's going to H-601 in Rehoboth. I've also flagged it as urgent for our pharmacist so they'll push to get Dr. Okafor's approval today. The pharmacist will handle getting the new prescription filled and ready for Eli before Sunday.
[turn 4] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Just a few pills to get him through, I'll pay cash, come on.
[turn 4] AGENT: I hear you, Kevin. I can't promise an emergency supply—that's a pharmacist decision based on state rules, and it only applies to non-controlled medications anyway. Vyvanse is a controlled substance, so that's not an option. What I can tell you is our pharmacist is working on getting Dr. Okafor's approval for the new prescription today, and that's your best path to get Eli covered before Sunday. The pharmacist will call if there's any issue.
[turn 5] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Can't you call the doctor? Like right now, get this moving faster?
[turn 5] AGENT: I can't make calls to the doctor myself, but our pharmacist will be reaching out to Dr. Okafor as part of the urgent flag I just set. That's the fastest way to get this moving. The pharmacist has the credentials and direct lines to handle it, so they're your best bet to speed this up.
[turn 6] CALLER: Alright, alright. So the pharmacist's calling today, and it'll be ready at the Rehoboth store before Sunday? That's the plan?
[turn 6] AGENT: The pharmacist is flagged to work on getting Dr. Okafor's approval today. Once the doctor approves the new prescription, H-601 in Rehoboth will fill it. I can't promise it'll be ready before Sunday—that depends on how quickly the doctor responds—but the urgent flag means our pharmacist will push to make it happen. If there's any holdup, the pharmacist will call you.
[turn 7] CALLER: Okay, fine. Just make sure someone calls me if there's a holdup, alright? I don't want to find out Sunday morning we're stuck.
[turn 7] AGENT: Absolutely, Kevin. The pharmacist has your information and will call if there's any issue getting the prescription approved or filled. You won't be left hanging on Sunday morning.
[turn 8] CALLER: Alright, I'm counting on that. Thanks for pushing it through today.
[turn 8] AGENT: You're welcome, Kevin. We've got this. Have a good rest of your vacation, and we'll get Eli taken care of.
[turn 9] CALLER: Alright, thanks. Bye.

JSON only.
